All hypothesis test will use a significance level of $\alpha= 0.05\, \text{or}\,(5\%)$. Round numerical answers to 2 decimals where necessary.

## Problem 1

The average (mean) rating for an Airbnb lodging is $\mu=4.8$ with a standard deviation of $\sigma=0.8$. A research team randomly selected $n=100$ Airbnb lodgings in their city and found that the average rating was $M=4.6$.

a.  Identify the population and the sample in this scenario. \vspace{1.5in}

b.  Suppose we take many different random samples of size $n=100$ and compute the mean of each sample. If we make a histogram of these means, what will be the shape of this histogram? \vspace{1.5 in}

c.  Suppose we average all the means from part (b) above. What would be the mean of these sample means (i.e., the expected mean)? How do you know? \vspace{1.5 in}

d.  What would be the standard deviation of the sample means (the standard error)? \vspace{1.5 in}

e.  What is the probability of observing a sample mean of at least 4.9? To find the probability, you may use statistics tables or the online applet available at <https://onlinestatbook.com/2/calculators/normal_dist.html>.

\vspace{1.5 in}

f.  Would you consider the sample mean of 4.6 to be unusual? Why or why not? \vspace{1.5in}

\clearpage

## Problem 2

Psychologists are interested in investigating whether adolescents who spend considerable time on social media differ in their attention span compared to the general adolescent population. In a study, a sample of $n=81$ adolescents who reported spending at least three hours per day on social media completed a standardized attention assessment. In the general population of adolescents, scores on this assessment have a mean of $\mu=100$ but the standard deviation is unknown. The sample of adolescents who spend considerable time on social media had an average attention score of $M=95.4$ and a standard deviation of $SD=16.8$.

a.  Conduct a hypothesis test (assume all assumptions are met) to determine if the average attention score for adolescents who spend considerable time on social media is significantly different from the general adolescent population. Show/explain all work. \vspace{4.5 in}

b.  Calculate the estimated effect size and interpret it in context. \vspace{1.2 in}

\clearpage

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Problem 3

Here is a sample paragraph taken from the results section of a research report. The study investigated the effect of a mindfulness program on anxiety scores among college students.

"A t-test was conducted to determine whether college students who participated in a mindfulness program had different anxiety scores compared to the general college student population. Results indicated that students who participated in the mindfulness program $(M = 42.60, SD = 8.50)$ reported significantly lower anxiety scores than the general population mean of 48, $t(24) = −3.18, p = .004$, $\text{Cohen's d} = −0.64$. These findings suggest that anxiety scores among students who participated in the mindfulness program were significantly lower than the population average."

Use the paragraph above to answer the following questions.

a.  How many participants were in the sample? How do you know? \vspace{1 in}

b.  Based on the paragraph, was this a one-sample or two-sample t-test? How do you know? \vspace{1 in}

c.  Based on the paragraph, state the null hypothesis that was tested. \vspace{1.2 in}

d.  Based on the paragraph, was the null hypothesis rejected or not? How do you know? \vspace{1.2 in}

\clearpage

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Problem 4

A website designer working for [GoFundMe](https://www.gofundme.com/) wants to investigate whether including a photograph of a person seeking financial assistance on a fundraising page influences the amount of money donors contribute. The designer suspects that photographs may help donors develop an emotional connection with the person seeking assistance, potentially encouraging them to donate more money.

To investigate this question, the designer conducts an experiment involving 60 fundraising campaign pages. The pages are randomly assigned to one of two conditions:

- ***Photo group:*** 30 fundraising pages include a photograph of the person seeking donations.

- ***No-photo group:*** 30 fundraising pages contain the same information but do not include a photograph.

Each page is presented to a different group of potential donors under similar conditions. The website records the average donation amount (in dollars) received per donor for each campaign page.

The results are summarized below:

|          |           |                         |
|:--------:|:---------:|:-----------------------:|
|  Group   | Mean (\$) | Standard Deviation (\$) |
|  Photo   |  \$38.50  |         \$12.00         |
| No Photo |  \$30.20  |         \$10.50         |

a.  Identify the *independent* variable and the *dependent* variable in this study. \vspace{1.5in}

b.  State the null and alternative hypotheses in words and in statistical notation.\vspace{1.5 in}

c.  Calculate the *observed difference* in means and the *standard error* (assume equal variances). \vspace{1.5in}

d.  Calculate the *test statistic*. \vspace{1.5in}

e.  Find the *P-value* and write the conclusion for the hypothesis test in context. Be sure to show/explain your work for finding the *P-value*. \vspace{1.5in}

f.  Calculate the estimated *effect size* and interpret it in context. \vspace{1.5in}
